blocks.prompt: 5 A radioactive substance has a half-life of 2 years. If the initial quantity is 200 grams and the exponential decay function is \(Q(t) = Q\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{h}}\), then find the remaining quantity after 6 years graphically?
blocks.explanation:
Radioactive decay: every half-life (here 2 years) the amount is halved.
We must find the amount left after 6 years, reading it from a graph.
Plan: put \(Q_0 = 200\) and \(h = 2\) into the formula, tabulate at multiples of 2 years, draw the curve, read the value at \(t = 6\) and check by calculation.
steps:
Given: half-life \(h = 2\) years, initial quantity \(Q_0 = 200\) g, \(Q(t) = Q_0\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t/h}\).
To find: \(Q(6)\), from the graph of \(Q(t)\).
Method: write the model with the numbers, make a table, plot a smooth curve and read off \(t = 6\).

Write the model
\[Q(t) = 200\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t/2}\]
Why: the constant in front is the initial amount (at \(t = 0\), \((\tfrac{1}{2})^0 = 1\), so \(Q(0) = 200\)), and \(h = 2\) is the half-life.

Make a table (t = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
\[t:\ 0,\ 2,\ 4,\ 6,\ 8,\ 10\]
\[Q:\ 200,\ 100,\ 50,\ 25,\ 12.5,\ 6.25\]
Why: multiples of the half-life make the power \(t/2\) a whole number, so each value is simply half of the one before.

Draw the graph
Scales: 1 square = 1 year on the t-axis, 1 square = 25 g on the Q-axis. Plot the points and join them with a smooth curve.
The curve starts at \((0, 200)\), falls steeply at first and then more and more slowly, getting closer to the t-axis without touching it.
Why: exponential decay never reaches zero; each 2 years removes half of what is left.

Read the answer from the graph
From \(t = 6\) on the horizontal axis go up to the curve, then across to the Q-axis: the reading is 25 g.
Why: this is what "graphically" asks for.

Check by calculation
\[Q(6) = 200\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3}\]
\[= 200 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = 25\]
Also: 6 years = 3 half-lives, \(200 \to 100 \to 50 \to 25\).
Why: the calculation agrees with the graph reading.
blocks.final_answer: After 6 years, \(25\) grams of the substance remain.

answer_figure.alt: Decay curve Q(t) = 200 (1/2)^(t/2) for t from 0 to 11 years through (0, 200), (2, 100), (4, 50), (6, 25), (8, 12.5) and (10, 6.25); dashed lines from t = 6 up to the curve and across to Q = 25.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the decay function as \(Q(t) = Q\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t/h}\), using the same letter Q for the initial quantity. It should read \(Q(t) = Q_0\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{t/h}\), where \(Q_0 = 200\) g is the initial quantity and \(h = 2\) years is the half-life. The answer key (book page 296) numbers this answer as "8" ("25 grams"); the value is correct.
